rules.sentence: Zishan et al. described that presence of fluid-fluid levels in the lesion was the most useful differentiating MRI feature between telangiectatic osteosarcoma and aneurysmal bone cyst.
As compared to 74% of the osteosarcomas demonstrating a fluid level, 95% of the bone cysts had the presence of fluid levels.
Also, only aneurysmal bone cysts had lesions that were completely filled with a fluid-fluid level.
The high alkaline phosphatase level frequently seen in osteosarcoma is not a feature of telangiectatic osteosarcoma.

On the other hand, the evaluation of platelet count, white cell count, lactate dehydrogenase, and alkaline phosphatase have been described for differentiating telangiectatic osteosarcoma from aneurysmal bone cysts.
The sarcomas had a higher value of platelet count, white cell count, alkaline phosphatase, and lactate dehydrogenase than the aneurysmal bone cysts.
